topic.title: Two Brothers Split One Shoe Factory Into Adidas and Puma

title: Adidas and Puma Were One Shoe Company, Run by Two Brothers
description:
Adidas and Puma started as one family shoe company: so how did it become two?
Two brothers in a small German town split their factory, and the town split with them.
Sources: adidas, PUMA (Dec 2025).
Based on public records and reporting. Not financial or legal advice.

lines.text: Adidas and Puma were one shoe company, run by two brothers.
Adi Dassler made the shoes. His brother Rudolf sold them, from one factory in a small German town.
Then the brothers fell out, and nobody ever settled why. So what happened to their factory?
They cut it in half. Adi named his side Adidas, after himself.
Rudolf's side became Puma, across the little river that runs through town.
The whole town took sides. People looked at your shoes before they talked to you. So which side won?
Today, Puma is the one falling behind. Its sales fell 13.1% last year, and it lost €645.5M.
And Adidas, on the other bank? Last year Puma sold just 29% as much as Adidas did.
Adidas or Puma: which side are your shoes on? Because once upon a time,

Facts: Puma sales EUR 7,296.2M, -13.1% (reported, euro terms) and net income EUR -645.5M confirmed on PUMA annual report 2025 results-of-operations page; adidas EUR 24,811M (adidas press release 503) confirmed by search on adidas' own FY2025 results release and annual report (report.adidas-group.com). Verify list: shoemaker/salesman, RUDA->PUMA, factories on opposite banks of the Aurach, feud cause never settled (History.com); 'bent necks' town split (NZ Herald, Taipei Times/AFP). 2025 is still the latest full year. Brother photo is Commons public domain; logos only identify. Disclaimer ends description; no advice, no blame. Notes: script currency USD while facts are EUR (gap_part/gap_whole format as $ but are not shown); document card lines are a paraphrase of the report, not a quote.
